data.title: Stock Picks: Ta Ann And CIMB Group
data.description:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has identified Ta Ann Holdings and CIMB Group Holdings as stocks to watch, with the former attempting to extend its rebound while the latter maintains a bullish technical setup.

In its technical analysis, RHB Research said Ta Ann was testing immediate resistance after recording a bullish candlestick, although a long upper shadow indicated strong selling pressure at RM5.20.

A breakout above this level could attract fresh buying interest and lift the counter towards the next resistance levels of RM5.50 and RM5.75.

However, a fall below the RM4.95 support would signal a bearish breakout and potentially resume its corrective movement.

Meanwhile, CIMB Group is poised to extend its upward momentum after breaking above the RM7.15 resistance on strong trading volume.

RHB Research said the counter had climbed above its 21-day simple moving average and formed a bullish candlestick, indicating that its positive technical setup remained intact.

The banking stock is now eyeing the next resistance levels of RM7.50 and RM7.80. However, a breach of the RM6.90 support would invalidate the bullish outlook.

Malayan Industrial Investment (KL:MI) shed 36 sen to RM4.95, while BLD Plantation (KL:BLDPLNT) lost 46 sen to RM13.82.

All share prices and trading volumes are based on the day’s top gainers and losers list.

data.title: Bursa Rally Cools As FBM KLCI Retreats From 1,581 Midday Level
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia pared most of its midday gains to close higher on Thursday, with the benchmark FBM KLCI adding 8.69 points or 0.56% to 1,570.98 after retreating from its morning session level of 1,581.17.

The benchmark index had climbed 18.88 points or 1.21% at midday, reaching an intraday high of 1,584.96. However, it subsequently gave up much of those gains to finish at 1,570.98, still above its opening level of 1,563.15.

The broader market also weakened in the afternoon, with the FBM70 falling 291.56 points or 1.82% to 15,768.93, reversing its midday gain of 0.63%.

The FBM Small Cap Index shed 187.05 points or 1.33% to 13,918.83, while the FBM ACE Index recorded the steepest decline, dropping 177.78 points or 3.83% to 4,461.11.

The FBM Emas slipped 14.24 points or 0.12% to 11,467.68, while the FBM100 edged down 4.35 points or 0.04% to 11,329.11.

Among sector indices, the Consumer Products and Services Index was among the few gainers, rising 3.02 points or 0.70% to 437.39. The Construction Index fell 8.02 points or 2.87% to 271.28, while the Energy Index lost 3.52 points or 0.48% to 732.08.

Nestle remained among the day’s strongest performers, gaining RM1.48 to RM95.60, while Batu Kawan added 98 sen to RM19.98. Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia rose 50 sen to RM13.06, followed by PPB Group, which gained 47 sen to RM8.89, and Kuala Lumpur Kepong, up 42 sen to RM21.48.

On the most actively traded list, Malayan Agriculture and General (MAG) remained unchanged at 16 sen, with 76.49 million shares traded.

CBHB fell 10.5 sen to 46 sen after recording 66.47 million shares in volume, while ZETRIX was unchanged at five sen with 62.90 million shares traded. Dagang NeXchange (DNEX) slipped half a sen to 41.5 sen, while BCG gained three sen to RM1.18.

The market data was recorded at 5pm on November 26, with prices delayed by 15 minutes.

data.title: Stock Today: Sunway Slips 1% Despite Stronger Property And Construction Profits
data.description:
Sunway Bhd shares fell nearly 1% on Thursday afternoon, trading lower following the group’s latest quarterly results, which showed a 7.1% year-on-year decline in third-quarter net profit despite stronger contributions from its property development and construction divisions.

As at 3.28pm, the stock was down 4 sen or 0.98% at RM4.06, compared with its last adjusted closing price of RM4.10. It opened at RM4.00 and traded between RM3.98 and RM4.13, with 2.32 million shares changing hands.

The share price movement came after Sunway reported a 7.1% decline in net profit to RM314 million for the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM338 million a year earlier, although revenue rose 18% to RM3 billion.

Its property development division recorded a 45.5% increase in profit before tax to RM80.1 million, while the construction segment’s profit before tax grew 13.3% to RM137.5 million.

For the first nine months of 2026, Sunway achieved property sales of RM3.4 billion, putting it on track to meet its full-year target of RM4.2 billion. Its unbilled property sales stood at RM8.2 billion.

The construction division also secured RM9.8 billion in new contracts during the nine-month period, lifting its outstanding order book to a record RM12.45 billion.

The group’s healthcare segment recorded quarterly revenue of RM738.3 million and profit before tax of RM119.1 million.

data.title: Consumer Stocks Steal The Show As Bursa Extends Its Winning Run
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia extended its recovery at midday on Thursday, with the benchmark FBM KLCI climbing 18.88 points or 1.21% to 1,581.17 as buying interest lifted heavyweight stocks.

The benchmark index traded between 1,563.15 and 1,584.96 during the morning session, while the broader market also advanced. The FBM70 gained 101.56 points or 0.63% to 16,162.05, while the FBM Emas rose 117.91 points or 1.03% to 11,599.83.

Among the leading gainers, Nestle added RM1.38 to RM95.50, while Batu Kawan rose 98 sen to RM19.98. Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia gained 54 sen to RM13.10, followed by Fraser & Neave Holdings, which advanced 46 sen to RM19.90.

Kuala Lumpur Kepong added 42 sen to RM21.48.

In the broader market, Malayan Agriculture and General (MAG) was the most actively traded counter, with 69.64 million shares changing hands, while the stock remained unchanged at 16 sen.

NexG Bina was among the most actively traded stocks, falling half a sen to 3.5 sen, while Yes Group shed half a sen to 17.5 sen. D&O Green Technologies rose half a sen to 42.5 sen.

Among the top losers, Boustead Plantations fell 46 sen to RM13.82, while Dutch Lady Milk Industries shed 26 sen to RM27.00. K Seng Seng Corporation declined 15 sen to RM4.52.

The midday recovery follows Wednesday’s rebound, when bargain hunting in oversold blue-chip stocks helped lift the FBM KLCI, although concerns over AI valuations and proposed US tariffs continued to weigh on investor sentiment.

data.title: Stock Today: KLK Gains 1.8% Despite RM118 Million FY2026 Loss
data.description:
Shares in Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK) rose 1.8% at 11.45am, gaining 38 sen to RM21.44, despite the plantation group’s reported net loss of RM118.4 million for the financial year ended September 30, 2026 (FY2026).

The counter opened at RM21.10 and moved between RM20.80 and RM21.64, with 151,900 shares traded. Its last closing price was RM21.06.

KLK reported a net loss for FY2026, reversing a net profit of RM817.3 million a year earlier, after recognising a RM1.61 billion non-cash impairment on its investment in Synthomer plc.

However, the group recorded a stronger fourth-quarter performance, with profit after tax and minority interests (PATAMI) surging to RM549.6 million from RM96 million a year earlier.

Quarterly revenue increased 19.7% year-on-year to RM7.54 billion, supported by stronger plantation contributions, improved manufacturing performance and lower losses from Synthomer.

Excluding the impairment and its share of equity losses in Synthomer, KLK would have recorded an adjusted PATAMI of RM1.67 billion for FY2026, up 66.3% from RM1 billion previously.

Despite the full-year loss, the board declared a final single-tier dividend of 40 sen per share, unchanged from FY2025.

data.title: Stock Today: CIMB Gains 1.54% After Third-Quarter Earnings, Special Dividend
data.description:
Shares in CIMB Group Holdings Bhd rose 1.54% in morning trade on Thursday following the banking group’s latest quarterly results and announcement of a special dividend.

As at 10.20am, CIMB gained 11 sen to RM7.23, compared with its last traded price of RM7.12 recorded previously. The counter opened at RM7.14 and moved between RM7.13 and RM7.26, with 2.32 million shares changing hands.

The buying interest came a day after CIMB reported a 9.5% year-on-year decline in net profit to RM1.89 billion for the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM2.07 billion a year earlier.

Quarterly revenue also fell approximately 8.5% to RM5.4 billion from RM5.9 billion, amid pressure on interest margins and weaker non-interest income.

For the first nine months of FY2026, however, the group recorded cumulative net profit of RM5.73 billion, with annualised return on average equity remaining at 11%.

CIMB also declared a special dividend of 5.5 sen per share, totalling RM596 million, as part of its RM2 billion capital return commitment to shareholders.

In a separate assessment, CGS International Securities maintained its Add recommendation on CIMB with an unchanged target price of RM9.60, citing tighter cost controls, dividend yields and potential benefits from an anticipated increase in the Overnight Policy Rate in 2027.

The research house said CIMB’s nine-month net profit was within expectations, accounting for 72.1% of its full-year forecast and 74.2% of Bloomberg consensus estimates.

data.title: Treasury Yield Slide Limits Dollar Gains Ahead Of Thanksgiving
data.description:
The US dollar was little changed in Asian trading on Thursday as declining Treasury yields offset demand for safe-haven assets amid fragile market sentiment and uncertainty over the artificial intelligence (AI) sector.

The US dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of six major currencies, was flat at 103.7 after slipping to a one-week low overnight.

The dollar’s retreat came as US equities recovered from steep losses and investors reassessed the outlook for interest rates following stronger-than-expected economic data.

OCBC FX strategist Sim Moh Siong said the risk-reward of pursuing further dollar gains had become less attractive, although expectations of a hawkish Federal Reserve would continue to support the currency.

“The risk-reward of chasing further USD gains looks less attractive, but hawkish Fed risks should keep the dollar supported,” he said.

He added that the dollar’s relationship with equities could remain volatile, caught between safe-haven demand and concerns that a deeper AI slowdown could weigh on US economic growth.

The latest US data, including higher-than-expected core personal consumption expenditures inflation in October and an upward revision to third-quarter gross domestic product growth, reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates by 25 basis points in December and again in early 2027.

However, Treasury yields declined across the curve, with the 10-year yield falling as much as 10 basis points to 4.8%, its lowest level in around two-and-a-half months.

The drop in yields provided some relief to currencies that had come under pressure. The Australian dollar recovered above US$0.66 to US$0.6635 after touching US$0.6557, its weakest level in almost a year.

Elsewhere, the yen gained 0.1% against the dollar to around 159.06, while the euro was little changed at US$1.097.

The dollar’s movement also came amid fresh US tariff proposals targeting goods from 14 major trading partners, with China facing the highest proposed rates.

The proposed duties are intended to address what Washington described as structural excess industrial capacity and market-distorting exports.

Trading conditions were expected to remain subdued, with most US markets closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving, leaving Asian markets without fresh US price action.

The Swiss franc eased after gaining 0.5% overnight on safe-haven demand, while the Canadian dollar held near a two-week high as oil prices advanced.

Brent crude futures settled 3.5% higher at US$94.61 a barrel after Yemen’s Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Arabia’s largest oil refinery.

Reuters

data.title: Asian Shares Rebound As Nvidia Concerns And US Tariffs Keep Investors Cautious
data.description:
Asian markets edged higher on Thursday as regional equities recovered some ground following Wall Street’s rebound, although concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) valuations and fresh US tariff proposals continued to weigh on sentiment.

Japan’s Nikkei gained 1.6% while South Korea’s benchmark index rose 1.9%. The MSCI index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan added 0.6%, although it remained down 9% for November.

The recovery followed a volatile session on Wall Street, where the S&P 500 and Nasdaq initially suffered steep losses before recovering much of their declines as investors shifted towards more defensive sectors.

US S&P 500 futures rose 0.5% while Nasdaq futures gained 0.4% early on Thursday.

Technology stocks remained under pressure, with Nvidia once again at the centre of investor concerns after S&P placed the chipmaker’s credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade, citing weaknesses in its management and board oversight.

Nvidia shares fell 3.9% to US$149.30 on Wednesday, leaving the stock well below its October peak of US$243.37.

The broader market recovery also came amid questions over whether the recent volatility in equities and doubts about the sustainability of AI-driven investment could influence central banks’ interest rate decisions.

US Treasury yields fell to multi-week lows on Wednesday despite an upward revision to third-quarter economic growth to 4.3% and core inflation of 3.3%.

The yield on 10-year US Treasuries stood at 4.848%, after touching an 11-week low overnight.

Although futures continued to imply a 98% probability of a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December, expectations of a larger half-point increase had faded.

Meanwhile, fresh US tariff proposals targeting 14 trading partners, including China, Japan and the European Union, added to concerns over inflation.

However, the proposed duties will not be imposed on top of tariffs introduced in July.

Capital Economics chief North America economist Stephen Brown said the latest announcement was less alarming than it appeared, with the increase in the effective tariff rate expected to be slightly lower than previously anticipated.

“The additional tariff burden is likely to be small, but will still provide a marginal boost to prices and keep core goods inflation firm into next year,” he said.

In currency markets, the US dollar index eased to 103.71 as Treasury yields declined, while the euro edged up to US$1.0973.

The dollar held steady against the yen at 159.14, with the possibility of Japanese intervention keeping the 160 level in focus.

In commodities, Brent crude rose 0.2% to US$94.81 a barrel, while US crude gained 0.6% to US$84.24 following concerns over potential Middle East supply disruptions after Yemen’s Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Arabia’s largest oil refinery.

Gold fell 0.4% to US$3,566 an ounce and remained down almost 8% for the month.

Reuters

data.title: Bursa Bargain Hunters Return, But AI Sell-Off And Trump Tariffs Keep Traders Wary
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia rebounded on Thursday as investors picked up oversold blue-chip stocks, although lingering concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) valuations and fresh US tariff proposals continued to weigh on sentiment.

The FBM KLCI rose 9.48 points to 1,571.77, supported by buying interest in banking stocks and selected heavyweight counters.

CIMB Group Holdings gained seven sen to RM7.19, Public Bank added five sen to RM4.60 while AmBank Group rose two sen to RM6.63.

SD Guthrie continued its upward momentum following the previous session’s rally, gaining three sen to RM6.03.

Among stocks that released their quarterly results after Wednesday’s close, Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia climbed 62 sen to RM13.18, Hengyuan Refining Company added 32 sen to RM2.99 while Gas Malaysia advanced 17 sen to RM5.54.

On the broader market, NexG Bina was among the most actively traded counters, falling half a sen to 3.5 sen. Yes Group gained half a sen to 18.5 sen, while NWE was unchanged at 18 sen.

Despite the recovery, investors remained cautious following another round of selling in AI-related shares on Wall Street and US President Donald Trump’s proposed tariffs on 14 major trading partners, including Malaysia, China, Japan and the European Union.

The proposed tariff ceilings range from 20% to 40%, although the actual rates are expected to reflect lower levels agreed under completed or ongoing trade deals.

On Wall Street, the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.62% to 23,585.80, recovering from losses of more than 4% earlier in the session. The S&P 500 shed 0.25% to 7,182.78, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.33% to 50,182.95.

Technology stocks remained under pressure amid concerns over increased regulatory scrutiny of the AI sector, although bargain hunting helped limit the broader market losses.

Apex Securities said stock-specific opportunities could emerge amid the ongoing corporate earnings season and the FBM KLCI’s phased expansion from 30 to 50 constituents.

“We maintain our view that the market is in the process of finding a bottom, with near-term volatility likely to persist before sentiment gradually recovers,” it said in a note.

data.title: AI Boom Uncertainty Supports Ringgit Against US Dollar
data.description:
The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Thursday as concerns over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence (AI) rally prompted investors to seek safer assets, Bernama reported.

At 8am, the local currency strengthened to 4.1135/1220 against the greenback from Wednesday’s closing rate of 4.1170/1220.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US dollar index (DXY) fell 0.10% to 103.708 points, despite US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation rising to 3.8% in October from 3.7% in September.

He also noted that US Treasury yields declined, with the two-year yield falling four basis points to 4.65% and the 10-year yield dropping seven basis points to 4.86%.

“The decline in US Treasury yields gives the impression that there was a flight-to-quality as markets were having doubts whether the AI boom will continue to support AI-related stock prices.

“As such, ringgit is expected to maintain its tight range trade today,” he told Bernama.

Against a basket of major currencies, however, the ringgit opened weaker.

It eased against the euro to 4.5125/5218 from 4.5036/5091 at Wednesday’s close, while slipping against the British pound to 5.3932/4044 from 5.3756/3821. It also edged lower against the Japanese yen to 2.5837/5892 from 2.5820/5853.

The local note traded mixed against its ASEAN peers, gaining against the Indonesian rupiah to 224.4/224.9 from 224.6/224.0.

However, it weakened against the Singapore dollar to 3.1880/1951 from 3.1858/1899 and the Thai baht to 12.0751/1093 from 12.0599/0798.

The ringgit was unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.46/6.48.

data.title: SGX Opens Lower With Wall Street’s AI Selloff Weighing On Sentiment
data.description:
Singapore shares opened lower on Thursday, with the Straits Times Index (STI) slipping 5.28 points, or 0.11%, to 4,925.55 as investors remained cautious following losses on Wall Street.

As at 9.05am, market breadth was positive, with 96 advancers against 41 decliners. Trading volume stood at 48.09 million securities, valued at S$86.05 million.

Among the STI constituents, DBS Group Holdings fell 0.11% to S$65.33, while OCBC Bank was quoted at S$26.34. Singtel traded at S$4.22, Seatrium at S$1.34 and UOB at S$35.24. ST Engineering stood at S$8.55, while Genting Singapore traded at S$0.525.

The cautious start followed a mixed session on Wall Street on Wednesday, where the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite ended lower amid continued selling in technology and artificial intelligence-related stocks.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 164.25 points, or 0.33%, to 50,182.95, while the S&P 500 fell 18.31 points, or 0.25%, to 7,182.78. The Nasdaq Composite declined 147.73 points, or 0.62%, to 23,585.80.

The Nasdaq had fallen more than 4% during the session before bargain hunting helped limit losses ahead of the US Thanksgiving holiday.

Technology and consumer discretionary stocks led declines among the S&P 500 sectors, with both falling 1%. Nvidia dropped 3.9% and Amazon lost 3.1%, while HP surged 11.5% after reporting better-than-expected quarterly results.

Investor sentiment also remained under pressure from concerns over proposed US tariffs on goods from 14 trading partners, alongside expectations that stronger economic growth and higher inflation could prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027.

data.title: Hang Seng Futures Face Another Leg Down After 22,000 Support Breaks
data.description:
Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) extended its decline on Wednesday, breaking below the key 22,000-point support level and reinforcing the bearish technical outlook, according to RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research).

The futures contract fell 274 points to close at 21,939 points after opening lower at 22,205 points. It traded between 21,916 and 22,519 points before ending the session with a fresh bearish candlestick.

In evening trading, the HSIF slipped another 82 points to 21,857 points.

RHB Research said the break below 22,000 points reaffirmed the bearish technical setup, with the Relative Strength Index (RSI) continuing to form lower lows, indicating that downward momentum remained intact.

The research house expects the HSIF to extend its decline towards the next support at 21,500 points, followed by 20,500 points. Immediate resistance is now placed at 22,500 points, with a stronger barrier at 23,000 points.

It therefore maintained a negative trading bias and advised traders to retain short positions initiated at 23,576 points, or at the Nov 13 close.

The stop-loss level remains fixed at 23,500 points.

data.title: Wall Street Closes Mixed As Bargain Hunting Limits AI-Driven Selloff
data.description:
Wall Street ended mixed on Wednesday, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite closing lower after an AI-related selloff, although bargain hunting helped both indexes recover from steeper intraday losses ahead of the US Thanksgiving holiday.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 164.25 points, or 0.33%, to 50,182.95, while the S&P 500 fell 18.31 points, or 0.25%, to 7,182.78. The Nasdaq Composite declined 147.73 points, or 0.62%, to 23,585.80.

The Nasdaq had fallen more than 4% earlier in the session as investors retreated from technology and artificial intelligence-related stocks amid renewed concerns over tariffs and the outlook for interest rates.

However, bargain hunters stepped in to take advantage of lower valuations, helping the major indexes recover from their session lows.

“There are all these potential headwinds, but then there’s also a certain amount of conditioning of buying on the dip, and that’s part of what we’re seeing,” said Oliver Pursche, senior vice-president and adviser for Wealthspire Advisors.

Technology and consumer discretionary stocks led declines among the S&P 500 sectors, each falling 1%, while materials and real estate were among the gainers.

Nvidia shares dropped 3.9%, while an index tracking semiconductor stocks declined 0.7%. Amazon also fell 3.1%.

On the other hand, HP shares surged 11.5% after the personal computer maker reported fourth-quarter revenue and profit above analysts’ estimates.

Investor sentiment remained under pressure following concerns over increased regulatory scrutiny of the AI sector after Democrats’ gains in the US midterm elections.

The Nasdaq Composite is down 7.3% for November, while the Nasdaq 100 briefly fell 20% from its record closing high during Wednesday’s session, approaching the threshold for a bear market.

Trade concerns also weighed on sentiment after the US proposed tariffs on goods from 14 trading partners to address what it described as structural excess industrial capacity.

Investors were also assessing stronger-than-expected US economic growth in the third quarter and higher inflation in October, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027.

The US stock market will be closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving and will close early on Friday.

Reuters

data.title: Stock Picks: 99 Speed Mart And Dagang NeXchange
data.description:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has identified 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd and Dagang NeXchange Bhd (DNeX) as stocks with bullish technical setups, citing breakouts above key resistance levels that could pave the way for further gains.

For 99 Speed Mart, RHB Research said the stock had staged a bullish breakout after closing above the RM3.10 resistance level following a bullish candlestick formation.

The research house said the counter could extend its upward movement towards the next resistance levels of RM3.25 and RM3.35, provided it remains above the breakout point.

However, a fall below the RM2.97 support level would invalidate the bullish setup and signal a resumption of downward movement.

Meanwhile, DNeX is also showing signs of sustained bullish momentum after climbing above its RM0.415 resistance level.

RHB Research said the counter’s positive price action could continue towards the next resistance levels of RM0.45 and RM0.48.

A breach below the RM0.39 support level would negate the bullish setup and potentially trigger another correction.

data.title: US Stocks Tumble On Hot Inflation, Trump Tariffs
data.description:
US stocks fell on Wednesday as chip stocks extended their sell-off, the Trump administration announced new 20% tariffs, and the PCE index showed price increases picked up in October.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1.5%, while the S&P 500 sank 2.3%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite tumbled 3.3%.

Markets are on weaker footing as a sell-off in semiconductor stocks continued, with Nvidia shares losing 8% in early trading. Despite Friday’s major rally on Jensen Huang’s Nvidia reinstatement, the AI trade has remained under pressure as questions about AI’s profitability hammer stocks.

The focus on Wednesday turned to the latest Personal Consumption Expenditures index data, which showed core PCE — the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge — rose to 3.3%, ahead of economists’ expectations of 3.2% inflation. The reading solidified bets that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in December, with traders pricing in a 98% chance of a 25 basis point hike next month.

data.title: Plantation Stocks Lead Gainers As MPI Tops Decliners
data.description:

United Plantations rose 28 sen to RM31.68, followed by Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK), which gained 26 sen to RM21.06.

Mentiga Corporation Bhd advanced 21 sen to RM1.53, while Bintulu Port Holdings Bhd and Lebtech Bhd each added 20 sen to RM5.20 and 79 sen, respectively.

On the downside, MPI led the decliners, falling RM1.20 to RM35.80, followed by Nestlé (Malaysia) Bhd, which shed 92 sen to RM94.12.

Dutch Lady Milk Industries Bhd declined 54 sen to RM27.26, while Greatech Technology Bhd and MI Technovation Bhd each lost 43 sen to RM2.07 and RM5.31, respectively.

The session saw buying interest concentrated in plantation counters, with United Plantations and KLK among the leading gainers. Meanwhile, technology and consumer stocks faced selling pressure, led by MPI and Nestlé.

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Edges Higher Despite Weak Market Breadth
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia bucked the regional trend to close marginally higher on Wednesday, supported by selective buying in heavyweight counters, particularly in the consumer products and services, plantation as well as transportation and logistics sectors.

At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 0.61 of a point, or 0.03%, to 1,562.29 from Tuesday’s close of 1,561.68.

The benchmark index opened 0.65 of a point lower at 1,561.03 before moving between an intraday low of 1,555.03 and a high of 1,565.17.

However, overall market sentiment remained weak, with decliners outnumbering advancers by 692 to 345. A total of 456 counters were unchanged, while 1,340 were untraded and 102 suspended.

Trading activity also eased, with total turnover declining to 2.53 billion shares valued at RM2.36 billion, compared with 3.26 billion shares worth RM3.07 billion on Tuesday.
